chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni, from al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said:

The Prophet (may God bless him and his family) would stand at the door of Ali and Fatima (peace be upon them both) at the break of every dawn and say: All praise is for God, the Doer of good, the Beautifier, the Bestower of favours, the Conferrer of benefits, through Whose grace righteous deeds are completed. Let a listener hear of the praise of God and His favour, and His trial is beautiful in our estimation.
We seek refuge in God from the Fire, we seek refuge in God from the mornings of the Fire, we seek refuge in God from the evenings of the Fire.
The prayer, O Ahl al-Bayt! "Indeed, God only desires to remove uncleanness from you, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification" [33:33].

key_terms.أهل البيت: Ahl al-Bayt, the People of the House — the Prophet's household, including Ali and Fatima
key_terms.الرجس: Uncleanness, impurity — in Quran 33:33 interpreted as spiritual impurity/sin
key_terms.الصالحات: Righteous deeds, good works — completed only through divine grace
key_terms.المحسن المجمل المنعم المفضل: Four divine attributes: the Doer of good, the Beautifier, the Bestower of favours, the Conferrer of benefits
key_terms.تطهيرا: Thorough purification — the absolute/emphatic form indicates complete spiritual purification

ai.seo_question: What was the daily practice of the Prophet at the door of Ali and Fatima?
ai.summary: This hadith records a daily devotional practice of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), who would stand at the door of Ali and Fatima (AS) every dawn to recite praises of God and call them to prayer. He would invoke four divine attributes — al-Muhsin, al-Mujmil, al-Mun'im, al-Mufdil — seek refuge from the Fire three times (morning, evening, and generally), and then call them to prayer while reciting the Verse of Purification (33:33). This practice, narrated through the Shia chain of Imams, is significant evidence for the special spiritual status of the Ahl al-Bayt.
